intended_object: The valuative relation (valuation class) on an algebraic extension M of a nonarchimedean local field K that extends the valuation of K, i.e. x ≤ᵥ y iff |x| ≤ |y| for the unique (spectral-norm) extension of the normalized absolute value of K (Neukirch II.4, II.6). Inferred from the docstring and module documentation.
explanation: The body equips M with Mathlib's spectral norm `spectralNorm.normedField K M`, built on the normalized absolute value of K (complete and ultrametric). It then applies `ValuativeRel.ofValuation` to `NormedField.valuation`, the valuation x ↦ ‖x‖₊ with values in ℝ≥0. So `vle x y` is ‖x‖₊ ≤ ‖y‖₊, which is ‖x‖ ≤ ‖y‖; the library proves this in `algebraicExtensionValuativeRel_vle_iff`. The file also proves that this relation extends the relation on K (`algebraicExtension_valuativeExtension`) and that it is the unique valuative relation on M doing so (`algebraicExtensionValuativeRel_eq`). It is therefore the canonical extended valuation class, and there are no degenerate-case problems. On generality: such an extension exists over any complete rank-one nonarchimedean valued field. Here, though, K carries only a `ValuativeRel`, and producing a real-valued norm from it uses the normalized absolute value, which needs the local-field structure (finite residue field, discrete valuation). The library works over local fields throughout. Mathlib has no general construction extending a valuative relation to algebraic extensions, and the general ingredients (spectralNorm.normedField, NormedField.valuation, ValuativeRel.ofValuation) are reused rather than rewritten.
